question.text: 'Kaveri Infrastructure Fund', a Category I Infrastructure AIF with investable funds of INR 500 crore, is evaluating a single deal of INR 140 crore in 'Deccan Highways Pvt Ltd'. Is this permissible under SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: Permissible — Cat I AIFs have a 50% single-investee limit
Not permissible — the Cat I investee-concentration cap is 10% of investable funds
Not permissible — Cat I/II AIFs cannot invest more than 25% of investable funds in a single investee; INR 140 cr = 28% > 25%
Permissible — Infrastructure Funds are exempt from concentration norms

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 15(1)(c): Category I and II AIFs cannot invest more than 25% of investable funds in one Investee Company, directly or through units of other AIFs. INR 140 cr / INR 500 cr = 28%, exceeds 25%. The 50% concession applies only to LVFs (Cat I/II). Cat III has a tighter 10% limit. The Trap: Option A is the LVF relaxation (Cat I/II). Option B applies the Cat III limit. Option D is fabricated — Infrastructure Funds have a 75%-in-unlisted-infra rule but no concentration exemption. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B test the 25%/10% split numerically. XIX-C adds LVF and IFSC carve-outs. Manager's Pro-Tip: Manager tip: 'Investable funds' is corpus net of estimated fund expenses over tenure — not the committed corpus. IC decks should show both committed-corpus and investable-funds concentration so LP advisory committee doesn't spring a breach mid-deployment. IFSC-domiciled Cat I/II are exempt from the 25% limit if PPM discloses this.
